email.subject1: a signal play for Datasaur partners
email.body1:
Nadya, saw Datasaur is scaling LLM Lab and automated labeling across names like Google, Netflix, and Spotify.

As partner-sourced demand grows, there are usually more co-sell accounts across the ecosystem than the team can cover by hand, and that is where partner pipeline goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Datasaur's partner ecosystem off hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Nadya, quick follow-up for Datasaur.

Partner-sourced pipeline usually stalls because nobody has time to personalize outreach to each partner's top accounts at scale, so co-sell motions quietly underperform.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to three of your top partner targets. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through them, plus how the same engine scales across your whole partner ecosystem without adding reps?
email.body3:
Nadya, last bit of proof for Datasaur.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how partner-sourced reply rates compare across AI and data software ecosystems. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Nadya, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling co-sell pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Growing a partner motion is its own kind of busy, and I get it.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page co-sell pilot playbook scoped to your partner ecosystem? I will tailor it to Datasaur either way.
